prose: CNBC frames Anthropic's IPO filing as a make-or-break moment for the whole AI trade. The company is being measured for a market cap in the trillions despite over $80 billion in first-half losses, with investors asked to focus on a 14-fold revenue increase. Neocloud and data-center stocks are already wobbling - Firmus and SK Hynix's Solidigm unit have withdrawn IPO plans.

The piece stresses Anthropic's entanglement with the megacaps: close to half its revenue comes from Claude sold through Microsoft, Amazon and Alphabet cloud divisions, which also hold stakes; some $77 billion in notes can be issued to Amazon, Broadcom and Google; Microsoft and Nvidia agreed to invest $15 billion; and Alphabet is backstopping a Texas data center. One VC warns that an underwhelming debut could make the sector look like 'a house of cards'.
highlights: Anthropic IPO seen as a test for the entire AI trade
Over $80B in first-half losses against 14x revenue growth
Nearly half of revenue comes via Microsoft, Amazon and Alphabet clouds
Firmus and Solidigm pulled IPOs as AI infrastructure stocks slide
